description: "paigasus-core main ruleset: required 'moon ci' check with strict up-to-date-branch policy; how that interacts with dependabot merge trains"

paigasus-core's `main` ruleset requires the `moon ci` status check with
`strict_required_status_checks_policy: true` (branch must contain latest main), plus
deletion/non-fast-forward protection. There is no required-review rule — `gh pr merge
--squash` works directly once checks are green and the branch is current.

**Why:** merging PRs in sequence invalidates the next PR's merge eligibility
(`mergeStateStatus: BLOCKED`, "base branch policy prohibits the merge") until its branch
contains the new main head.

**How to apply:** for dependabot merge trains, merge one PR, then wait — dependabot
auto-rebases its remaining PRs onto new main (check `headRefOid` changed) and `moon ci`
re-runs; merge when green. BUT dependabot stops rebasing a branch once anyone else pushes
to it — then use `PUT /repos/.../pulls/N/update-branch` (GitHub-signed merge of main into
the branch) and wait for the re-run. Its `expected_head_sha` must be the FULL 40-character SHA:
a short SHA returns HTTP 422 "expected head sha didn't match current head ref" (PR 329,
2026-09-27). The same call also works for your own feature PR right after `gh pr create`, and it
avoids a local rebase that would re-sign every commit. Watch main after each merge: push-to-main triggers
`CI`, `prebuild`, and sometimes `Dependency Graph`.

**`gh pr update-branch --rebase` is the right tool** (avoids a merge commit, so the commitlint
parity gate only ever sees dependabot's own commit) — **but it makes dependabot REGENERATE the
PR**, re-resolving deps to newest-available and blowing past the npm cooldown. See
[[pnpm-minimum-release-age]] for the resulting catch-22 and its fix.

A full 7-PR train (2026-08-05) took ~6 serial CI cycles at ~10-20 min each. The local
`.lefthook/pre-push/check-branch.sh` enforces `^feature/[a-z0-9._-]+$` (no Linear key
required; `main` and `dependabot/*` are exempt) and validates the CURRENT branch name — so to
push a fix onto a dependabot branch, rename the local branch to match it first.

**update-branch can leave `rs/Cargo.lock` stale** (PR 412, 2026-10-19): main moved `syn` to
3.0.9, the GitHub merge kept the PR's `pyo3-macros` entries on `syn 3.0.6`, and `--locked`
then failed the lockfile-integrity step and `build + smoke`. Fix: run `cargo metadata` in `rs/`
on the merged branch and commit the lock. Check this after every update-branch on a cargo PR.

Related: [[paigasus-commit-signing-1password]] (API-commit fallback when 1Password is locked),
[[dependabot-cargo-lockfile-truncation]] (never merge a cargo PR without checking its lock).

Measured 2026-09-24/25 on SMA-514 (PR 303, merged as 13c9c5f7). Four traps cost four CI runs of about 15 min each.

1. **Keycloak SSO after a console login: FIXED on the kind stack by SMA-682 (PR 375, merged 2026-10-04).** With `offline_access` granted (package default + a DEFAULT client scope), Keycloak issues an offline token and keeps no SSO session: the next `prompt=none` returns `login_required`, although the browser still holds KEYCLOAK_IDENTITY/SESSION (measured on 26.7.4, spec § 13 M5 and bite 2). The kind realm now makes `offline_access` OPTIONAL and `ci/kind/values/a.yaml` sets `oidc.scopes: openid profile email`; J1 steps 4 and 7 prove the session and its end. The package e2e realm still keeps `offline_access` default on purpose (D5), so that suite has NO SSO session. Also measured: the RFC 7009 revoke in `handleLogout` ALONE ends the SSO session (M6), so end-session never sees a live session on the kind stack. A bite that restores the old kind realm must keep the `/kind-sso-probe` redirect URI, or Keycloak answers the probe with HTTP 400.
2. **Logout confirmation page depends on a live SSO session.** RP logout with `client_id` and no `id_token_hint` shows "Do you want to log out?" ONLY while an SSO session is alive. On the kind stack the logout revoke already ends the session (point 1), so no page appears either way; J1's D8 check cannot prove what the SMA-681 hint does (SMA-682 residual R7).
3. **A local Keycloak spike that stops at the redirect is not the real flow.** It never exchanges the code, so it cannot reproduce point 1. Reproduce with the code exchange and the console's exact scopes.
4. **Playwright 1.63: `context.route` never sees a server-side redirect hop** (only the first request and direct gotos). To assert that `requireSession` refused a sid, check the redirect chain (first hop carried the cookie + 3xx to `<zone>/auth/login`), not a route stop.

Also: `kubectl logs -l <selector>` defaults to `--tail=10`; use `--tail=-1` in evidence collection. Keycloak logs no auth events at INFO — a diagnostic run needs `KC_LOG_LEVEL` with `org.keycloak.events:debug` and realm `eventsEnabled`.

**How to apply:** before a kind E2E fix loop, reproduce on the full console flow, not a direct IdP flow. Throwaway branches must match the pre-push hook `feature/[a-z0-9._-]+` (e.g. `feature/sma-NNN-throwaway-x`); never `--no-verify`. Related: [[paigasus-auth-two-tab-e2e-flake]], [[coderabbit-rate-limit-retrigger-futile]].
